title: A novel enzymatic assay for the identification of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase modulators
protocol: Thaw the protein on ice.
Dilute the protein to 7.5 μM with lysis buffer.
Pipette 10 μL of iron (II) solution into each well.
Add 110 μL of reaction buffer into each well.
If an HPPD modulator is being used, add 108.5 μL of reaction buffer and 1.5 μL of the modulator instead.
Add 10 μL of prepared protein to each well.
For a negative control, add 10 μL of lysis buffer to one or more wells without adding protein.
Mix the solution using a multichannel pipette.
Add 10 μL of ascorbate solution to each well.
Mix the solution again using a multichannel pipette.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil.
Incubate the plate for 30 min at 37°C.
While the plate incubates, create dilutions of the 4-HPP solution ranging from 0–30 mM.
Prepare a stock solution of 4-HPP at a concentration of 30 mM the day before.
Dilute the 4-HPP stock solution to the desired concentrations for the experiment.
Set up the reaction by adding 4-HPP (12 mM) into the protein mixture, achieving a final concentration of 0.8 mM.
Initiate the reaction and incubate at the specified conditions for 2 hours.
Add modulator at the desired concentration if conducting experiments with HPPD modulators.
If the modulator is dissolved in DMSO, dissolve it using 1.5 μL DMSO and mix the solution.
Initiate the reaction by adding the modulator to the solution.
Add 10 μl of substrate solution at the desired concentration and mix the solution.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil.
Incubate for 2 h at 37°C.
End the enzymatic reaction.
Remove the tray from the incubator and place it into a fume hood.
Add 150 μL of methanol to each reaction well.
Mix the solution.
Centrifuge at 2100xg for 15 min, at 4°C.
Transfer 50 μL of the clear solution from each well to a corresponding well of a new microplate.
Add 100 μL of borate solution into each well.
Mix the solution thoroughly.
Record a first reading using a plate reader at 306 nm.
Seal the plate with an aluminum seal film and cover it entirely in foil.
Read the absorbance at 306 nm every hour for 16 hours.
Reseal the plate between readings to prevent methanol evaporation.
Note that in the absence of 4-HPP, absorbance readings of experimental run (+HPPD) and blank (-HPPD) should overlap.
Plot one of the 4-HPP concentrations to observe differences between experimental run and blank.
At 0.8 mM of 4-HPP, the experimental run and blank demonstrate clear differences.
For HTS experiments, use single point readings at time point 16 h.
If available, use an HPPD inhibitor (e.g., NTBC) as a positive control.
